cards.headline: Death toll from Russian strike on Zaporizhia aid center rises to at least 50

pages.text: The death toll from a Russian attack on an aid distribution center in the village of Komyshuvakha, located in Ukraine’s Zaporizhia region, has risen to at least 50 people. The strike is among the deadliest Russian attacks in the region. Ukraine’s emergency service reported the toll increased after rescuers recovered eight more bodies from the rubble. Acting regional governor Mykhailo Semikin later stated the death toll reached 53 people, though Al Jazeera was not able to independently verify that figure. On November 4, 2026, local police reported that 59 people were listed as missing, noting that some of those individuals might be among the bodies already recovered. Officials stated that as many as 39 people may still remain trapped under the debris. As rescuers continue their search for missing bodies for the fifth day, specialists are taking DNA samples to identify the deceased. Ongoing Russian attacks have remained a constant threat to the rescue operation.

Ukraine reported that on November 2, 2026, Russian aircraft bombed a former school near the front lines that civilians were using for weekly aid handouts. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated on X that after an initial aerial bomb strike, a second wave of nine more bombs hit the underground shelter where people had taken cover, causing most of the destruction.

cards.headline: Somalia's Supreme Court rules President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term extension unlawful

pages.text: Somalia's Supreme Court ruled on November 5, 2026, that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud unlawfully extended his presidential term, a decision that has escalated a political crisis and a standoff between the presidency and the judiciary. The court determined that constitutional changes approved by parliament in March could not be applied retrospectively to the president's current term. While Mohamud's four-year mandate expired in May, his administration had extended it by one year, declaring a “transition period” to prepare for the country’s first nationwide democratic elections. The court stated that Mohamud should have left office in May. The ruling follows opposition accusations that the president used constitutional changes to prolong his rule, a move that sparked violent protests in the capital, Mogadishu. President Mohamud has maintained that the reforms are necessary to transition Somalia away from a clan-based system, where elders select representatives, toward fully democratic elections. Somalia last held nationwide direct elections in 1969 and has experienced civil war for more than 30 years, while the Islamist militant group al-Shabab continues to control many rural areas.

The Supreme Court's ruling coincided with a separate decision declaring the dismissal of Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed as “null and void.” The court accused the presidency of interfering with judicial independence, asserting that the chief justice could only be removed through established constitutional procedures. This ruling came one day after Mohamud dismissed Ahmed on November 4, 2026. The presidency stated the dismissal followed complaints regarding the administration of justice and was intended to achieve a transparent judiciary. Following the dismissal, Mohamud appointed Ibrahim Idle Suleiman, who previously held the position, to replace Ahmed. Unconfirmed reports indicate that Ahmed is under arrest. In its ruling, the court ordered political leaders to agree on an electoral plan within 30 days and to hold elections within 90 days, a mandate that potentially disrupts government plans for nationwide polls.

cards.headline: US Attorney Jason Reding Quinones resigns from Justice Department

pages.text: Jason Reding Quinones, the US Attorney for the Southern District of Florida, has submitted his resignation from the United States Department of Justice (DOJ), according to Attorney General Todd Blanche. Quinones, described as a Trump loyalist, had overseen and expanded a federal government probe into alleged Russian support for Donald Trump’s 2016 election campaign. While a special investigator later determined there was no direct collusion between the Trump campaign and Russia, the president has characterized the probe as a political “witch-hunt.”

During the investigation overseen by Quinones, former CIA director John Brennan, former Director of National Intelligence James Clapper, and former FBI Director James Comey were reportedly subpoenaed, though no charges were filed against them. Separately, Comey was indicted over a social media post that prosecutors alleged was a threat against the president in April. Court filings suggest the DOJ is also seeking to prosecute Comey for allegedly leaking classified information. A judge dismissed an earlier case against Comey in November. Comey has described the efforts to prosecute him as an “appalling abuse of the Department of Justice.”

Quinones also oversaw the US indictment of 94-year-old Cuban revolutionary Raul Castro during a Trump administration pressure campaign against the Communist-led nation. In a post regarding the resignation, Attorney General Blanche stated, “We are grateful for Jason’s leadership in combatting violent crime, drug trafficking, sex trafficking, and transnational crime, including the indictment of Raul Castro.” Quinones' departure follows a Democratic victory in the midterm elections as the administration prepares for Democrat-led investigations.

cards.headline: Sweden Democrats drop demands for ministerial posts amid government formation gridlock

pages.text: The far-right Sweden Democrats party has announced it is dropping its demands for ministerial posts, a move that potentially increases the chances for Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson to remain in power. Sweden Democrats leader Jimmie Akesson stated that, following the election outcome, his party will remain outside of the government for the next four years and is prepared to “tolerate” the formation of a center-right cabinet. The party has been an ally of the current right-wing caretaker government. Following a September election, Kristersson’s bloc lost its majority but was tasked by Sweden’s parliament speaker with exploring how to form a government because the center-left election winners failed to agree on a coalition.

The Center Party holds a pivotal role in determining whether Sweden forms a right-wing or left-wing government. The party has ruled out supporting any cabinet that includes the Sweden Democrats, and it has also ruled out supporting a cabinet that includes the Left Party. While the Center Party has expressed a preference for Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson to serve as prime minister, there is currently no indication that the party will back a government led by Kristersson. The Center Party did not provide an immediate comment regarding the Sweden Democrats' decision.

Parliament Speaker Andreas Norlen is widely expected to return the mandate to Andersson if Kristersson fails to secure a majority. If no solution to the current gridlock is found, Sweden could face a new election.

cards.headline: South Africa's ANC headed for all-time election low with nearly 32% of votes

pages.text: First results from local government polls in South Africa indicate the African National Congress (ANC) is headed for its worst-ever election performance. After 80% of the votes had been counted, the election authority dashboard showed the ANC, which remains the largest party, held nearly 32% of the votes. This follows a decline from the party's previous results, including just over 40% at the 2024 national polls and 46% at the 2021 municipal elections. In 2004, the party of Nelson Mandela secured nearly 70% of the national vote.

The municipal elections were dominated by concerns regarding failing water and power supplies. The electoral commission reported that approximately 15.9 million of 29.2 million registered voters cast ballots, resulting in an estimated 54.5% turnout. This turnout is up from 46% during the 2021 local elections. Political analyst Daniel Silke told AFP that the result is the ANC's worst in history and could undermine its ability to exert authority at both local and national levels. Silke suggested opposition parties may gain momentum ahead of the 2029 general election.

cards.headline: White House denies reports that Hegseth and Rubio will leave administration roles

pages.text: The White House and the US State Department have dismissed reports that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth might leave their positions following Republican election losses. The White House and State Department characterized reports of Rubio's potential departure as “fake news.” In an interview with The New York Times, Rubio stated that working for Donald Trump until the end of his term has “always been my plan” and added, “I love the work I’m doing.” Rubio is also denying reports that he is considering leaving his post in preparation for a 2028 presidential run. While Rubio has denied these reports, Defence Secretary Hegseth faces a more uncertain political future. US media have reported calls to replace Hegseth, specifically regarding his handling of the Iran war, which Donald Trump and Vice-President JD Vance have both blamed for Republican losses that resulted in Democrats gaining full control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate.

One outgoing congressional Republican has threatened to force an impeachment vote against Hegseth. In response, Hegseth posted a video statement defending his record and denouncing the efforts to remove him. “You see, they attack me. They attack us because we are effective,” Hegseth said in the video, adding, “It's not going to work. We will not back down.”

cards.headline: Yemen’s UN-recognised government dismisses ministers and officers following Houthi advances

pages.text: The UN-recognised government of Yemen has implemented a series of dismissals and appointments across its political and military leadership. The shake-up follows Houthi victories, including the loss of territory in September, and an ongoing four-week siege of Taiz, the country’s third largest city. The government is attempting to regain lost territory and address pressure from southern Yemenis for increased political power. This leadership change comes as a counteroffensive launched on 5 October, which aimed to liberate the entire country from Houthi control, has failed amid fighting that has left thousands dead on both sides. On 2 November 2026, Reuters reported that Houthi forces were approximately 37 miles (60km) from Aden, the nominal seat of the UN-recognised government.

cards.headline: Syria and Saudi Arabia sign defense and reconstruction deals

pages.text: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman signed a defense cooperation deal and a contract for Syria's participation in Expo 2030 Riyadh on November 4, 2026. The defense pact, signed during al-Sharaa's visit to Riyadh, includes advisory support, training, and the exchange of expertise between the two nations. Additionally, the signed contract for Expo 2030 marks an advanced stage in Syria's preparations to develop pavilion plans and visitor programs for the exhibition.

Two Syrian military sources and a senior US official stated that Syria is providing military advice and training to Saudi Arabia as the kingdom faces attacks from Yemen's Houthis. The senior US official said advisers and training teams from Syria, where fighters have become battle-hardened through years of war, have been traveling to Saudi Arabia to help train Saudi and Yemeni units to improve combat effectiveness. The two Syrian military sources, who have direct knowledge of the matter, said scores of military personnel had traveled from Syria to Saudi Arabia in recent weeks for advisory and training work, noting their mandate could be broader. Saudi Arabia has been involved in worsening hostilities with the Iran-allied Houthis since July, following the reignition of the Yemen war due to the wider conflict in the Middle East.

A senior Syrian diplomat described suggestions of military deployments as premature, stating that Syria's focus remains on reconstruction, protecting its borders, and internal security. However, a senior Saudi official told Reuters that while ongoing expertise sharing is mainly intended to restructure Syrian forces, Syrian partners may also assist with combat experience regarding fighting militias. The Saudi official added that joint training exercises are currently underway, with more planned for both security and defense.

cards.headline: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns following Ueno Bank collapse

pages.text: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigned after a financial and political crisis involving the collapse of Ueno Bank's banking system triggered widespread protests and impeachment proceedings. Peña, a 47-year-old economist in power since August 2023, announced his decision in a video posted to X as lawmakers debated his impeachment. He stated he was stepping down in the interest of the country's stability, social peace, and the need to preserve democratic institutions, adding an apology to the people if he had failed them. Minutes after the announcement, the Chamber of Deputies voted 78-0 to impeach him, sending the charges to the Senate. While congressional leaders were expected to accept the resignation to allow Vice President Pedro Alliana to be sworn in, opposition senators demanded a trial to prevent Peña from potentially retaining legal protections that could prevent prosecution. Peña, a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, had previously held a stake in a company related to Ueno Bank. The crisis has impacted Paraguay's currency, with the guaraní falling nearly 4% against the U.S. dollar, bringing its total losses to nearly 7% according to central bank exchange-rate data.

The crisis centers on Ueno Bank, which grew from an obscure finance company to one of Paraguay's largest lenders, claiming more than 60% of the country's adult population as customers. On November 2, 2026, the central bank ordered Ueno into resolution over insolvency, and on November 3, 2026, the central bank seized the lender citing a severe capital shortfall. This action froze the deposits of approximately 3 million customers, leaving hundreds of thousands of families without access to money for food and basic daily expenses. Regulators investigating the bank found poorly documented lending and expenses that were wrongly accounted for as assets. Once the books were corrected, Ueno's capital fell more than half below the legal minimum. The bank's app, cards, and transfers went dark, and its branches locked their doors. On November 4, 2026, a rush to open new accounts elsewhere caused other banks' mobile apps to crash. The collapse has left 7,000 employees facing unpaid wages and has impacted depositors, retirees, and government pensions, as Ueno reportedly held roughly $800 million in public deposits, which accounted for about a quarter of its total.

Ueno Bank's rapid expansion occurred after it received authorization from the central bank to operate as a digital bank at the end of 2023. The bank attracted customers through generous cash-back offers on groceries and by sponsoring Paraguay's national football team. Critics and protesters have questioned how the bank grew so quickly despite warnings regarding its lending practices. In June, central bank inspectors found a pattern of risky lending to insiders, including large sums extended to companies tied to the bank's owners without sufficient collateral. On a single day in September 2025, nearly $39 million went to three such companies. Peña had previously defended Ueno and the central bank's oversight, dismissing concerns as a smear campaign. The crisis also turned Peña's own Colorado Party against him; party leader and former President Horacio Cartes backed impeachment, stating the party would not side with the plundering of public and private funds and pensioners' money. On November 4, 2026, players from the national football team released a letter demanding a forceful response from the government and the justice system.

cards.headline: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years for murder of 190 children and one adult

pages.text: Paul Mackenzie, the leader of the Good News International church, has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in Kenya. A court in the coastal city of Mombasa delivered the sentence, which consists of 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years for direct homicide. The ruling came two weeks after the court found Mackenzie guilty of the crimes, which occurred between January 2021 and September 2023. Mackenzie's lawyer stated he would appeal the decision. Mackenzie also faces separate trials for manslaughter and terrorism charges, which he denies. He had previously denied the murder charges, arguing he did not force victims to starve, but the court rejected that defense. Twenty-eight accomplices convicted alongside Mackenzie were also sentenced to various prison terms. Prosecutors had called for the death penalty, though Kenya has not carried out an execution since 1987.

The convictions stem from a doomsday sect that ordered followers to starve themselves and their children to death to meet Jesus before the world ended. According to prosecutors, Mackenzie's followers were also subjected to threats and beatings by accomplices to ensure they followed these orders. The movement reportedly denounced formal education as satanic and viewed modern medicine and hospitals as instruments of the devil, requiring members to cut themselves off from the outside world. The victims' emaciated bodies were discovered in the Shakahola forest near the coast in southeastern Kenya, where they had been scattered in shallow graves, dumped in latrines, or, in some cases, buried alive. Authorities began uncovering these bodies in 2023 following a tip-off that led to Mackenzie's arrest in April 2023. Since the discovery of the mass graves, more than 400 bodies have been recovered, though many were severely decomposed and only 26 could be identified.

The Shakahola tragedy has prompted nationwide scrutiny regarding religious violence and the government's ability to monitor such groups. Investigations revealed that Mackenzie had been on the radar of authorities since 2017, when police searched his premises, and he had been arrested twice in the past before being released. The scale of the deaths in the Shakahola forest is comparable to other major cult disasters, such as the 2000 Ugandan doomsday cult that killed more than 700 people and the 1978 Jonestown massacre in Guyana, where more than 900 people died. Following the discovery of the graves, there have been calls for the Kenyan government to impose stricter regulations on religious organizations.

cards.headline: Google, Meta, and TikTok sue California to block law targeting social media addiction in minors

pages.text: Google, Meta, and TikTok filed separate lawsuits on November 4, 2026, to block a California law intended to limit the risk of addicting children under 16 to social media platforms. The companies filed the suits in federal courts in San Francisco, Los Angeles, and San Jose, naming California Attorney General Rob Bonta as the sole defendant. The legal challenge seeks to prevent the enforcement of Assembly Bill 1709, which was signed by Governor Gavin Newsom on 10 September. The law is scheduled to take effect on 1 January 2027, unless a judge voids it or puts it on hold. The office of Rob Bonta said on November 5, 2026, that it was reviewing the lawsuits and remains committed to defending the state's laws to protect children online.

Assembly Bill 1709 prohibits social media platforms from offering underage children “psychologically exploitative features” that could lead to compulsive use. These prohibited features include providing personal recommendations and sending videos through autoplay features. The law also requires platforms to implement “reasonable measures,” such as verifying users' ages, to ensure those under 16 do not access addictive features, and mandates the deletion of children’s accounts that utilize such features. Governor Newsom stated that children’s safety should be central to technology discussions and that California will not allow unregulated technology to put children at risk.

The tech companies argue the law violates the U.S. Constitution’s First Amendment free speech protections and Section 230 of the federal Communications Decency Act, a law that broadly shields online platforms from liability regarding content posted by their users. TikTok described the law as an unconstitutional restriction on free expression that erodes the practice of curating content based on user preferences. Meta stated the law violates the First Amendment by allowing the government to dictate how ideas are organized, displayed, or shared, noting that the company might be forced to either remove age-appropriate features or cut California teens off from their communities. Google, which owns YouTube and is a unit of Alphabet, argued that the law breaks systems built to help children find high-quality, age-appropriate videos. Google spokesperson José Castañeda said parents are best positioned to make decisions for their families.

cards.headline: Vice President JD Vance attributes Republican midterm losses to opposition to Iran war

pages.text: Vice President JD Vance stated that the primary reason for the Republican Party's dramatic losses in the U.S. midterm elections was the American public's opposition to the ongoing conflict with Iran. Writing on X the morning after the election, Vance suggested that any honest discussion regarding the party's future must begin with the war. He challenged those who might argue the conflict was worth the political cost, noting that the party lost the Senate for the next six years. This conflict began in late February 2026 following U.S.-Israeli airstrikes against Iran in the Middle East. While Vance's public critique of administration policy is noted as rare, President Donald Trump stated he did not disagree with Vance's assessment that frustration with the war influenced voters. However, Trump continued to defend the conflict, telling reporters, “The Iran thing, we had to do and we continue to do it.”

The future of the conflict remains uncertain as the administration faces political and military complexities. While Trump has defended the necessity of the war, the U.S. military has reportedly been preparing options and increasing capabilities in the Persian Gulf region in the event the president directs a resumption of hostilities. This comes as the conflict has caused setbacks for the regime in Tehran but has not achieved the officially stated strategic goals, such as forcing regime change or militarily defeating perceived threats to U.S. assets and allies. Additionally, the war has been associated with rising fuel costs for Americans. Looking ahead to January, the administration may face a Democratic Congress that is almost uniformly opposed to the war. Some officials in Washington, referred to as Iran war hawks, argue that pulling back now could allow Iran to rebuild before the conflict is won and would render previous military and reputational costs wasted.

cards.headline: Canada budget proposes more than $50 billion to expand electricity system

pages.text: The Canadian federal government's Budget 2026 outlines a plan to spend more than $50 billion in the coming decades to expand the nation's electricity system. This funding is part of an ambitious goal set by the Carney government to double Canada's electricity grid by 2050. Increasing the production and distribution of clean power is intended to help achieve Canada's net-zero climate goal and decarbonize the economy. The government expects these measures to cost $2.4 billion this decade, followed by $36.1 billion over fiscal years 2031-32 to 2041-42. According to Ottawa's finalized electricity strategy, the federal government is spending a total of $115 billion in electrification through 2041-42. Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne stated in prepared remarks that the government intends to connect provincial grids, build thousands of kilometres of transmission lines, and develop the nuclear energy sector, noting that countries with abundant electricity will lead the 21st century.

Much of the proposed funding will be directed into existing investment tax credits. To improve the connection between provincial electricity grids, the government is expanding its clean electricity investment tax credit to help cover the costs of the highest-voltage intraprovincial electricity lines in each province. Additionally, the clean electricity investment tax credit and a separate credit for clean technology are being extended from 2034 to the end of 2040. The expansion of the grid is intended to meet rising demand as Canadians transition from gas-powered cars to electric vehicles, use energy-efficient heat pumps for home heating and cooling instead of fossil-fuel-based furnaces, and support energy-intensive artificial intelligence infrastructure.

cards.headline: Former lawmaker sentenced to 12.5 years in Macao's first national security case

pages.text: A Macao court sentenced 69-year-old former pro-democracy lawmaker Au Kam San to 12.5 years in prison following a closed-door trial. This marks the first publicly known prosecution under Macao's national security law since the law was enacted in 2009. Macao is a former Portuguese colony that has operated as a special administrative region since its return to Chinese rule in 1999. The case has raised concerns regarding judicial fairness and reflects Beijing's emphasis on security and intolerance of dissent, according to critics. While Macao's pro-democracy movement has not been as influential as the movement in neighboring Hong Kong, this verdict represents a significant application of national security legislation in the Chinese casino hub.

The court found Au guilty of subverting state power, breaching confidentiality, and establishing contact with organizations, groups, or people outside Macao to commit acts endangering national security. According to a court statement, Au assisted and cooperated with unspecified hostile organizations outside Macao over a long period of time to collect and disseminate political views containing ideas of subverting state power and false information. The court stated that these parties conspired to incite hatred among Macao residents against the central government with the intent to overthrow and undermine the country's fundamental system. Although the court noted Au is a first-time offender who admitted to a considerable portion of the criminal facts, the statement said he demonstrated a high degree of intent and that the potential consequences of his crimes are very serious.

Au's family has challenged the legitimacy of the proceedings. His wife, Virginia Cheang, described the case in a public letter as a political trial and groundless persecution intended to humiliate his character, questioning the transition from a closed-door trial to a public verdict. She stated she hopes authorities will allow the family to visit Au and exchange letters without conditions. Au's daughter, Au Hon I, told The Associated Press that her father is a peaceful family man who cares deeply about Macao, expressing that the prospect of him spending time in prison without having done anything criminal is unbearable.

cards.headline: Ghanaian Minority demands probe into Akamai shutdown of digital health systems over US$64,510.95 debt

pages.text: The Minority in Parliament has demanded an investigation into the suspension of critical electronic health information systems in Ghana after technology services provider Akamai suspended ten servers due to an outstanding payment of US$64,510.95. Dr Nana Ayew Afriye, the Ranking Member of Parliament’s Health Committee, stated in a November 6, 2026, press release that the Ghana Health Service (GHS) disclosed in a November 2 communication that critical systems, including the District Health Information Management System (DHIMS2), had been inaccessible since October 29. The Minority says the disruption raises questions regarding the government’s financial planning, contract management, and oversight of the nation's digital health infrastructure.

The shutdown occurred despite government efforts to increase national control over health data. In October 2025, Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh announced the introduction of the Ghana Health Information Management System (GHIMS) to replace the Lightwave Health Information Management System (LHIMS). While GHIMS and DHIMS2 perform different functions, the Minority considers both part of Ghana’s wider digital health ecosystem and expressed concern regarding the sustainability of the government's digital health strategy. The caucus criticized the Ministry of Health and the GHS for allowing unpaid contractual obligations to disrupt national health information systems, and questioned Akamai's decision to suspend services despite potential public health consequences, while acknowledging that contractual obligations must be respected.

The Minority is also questioning the allocation of resources for digital health transformation. They noted that the Ministry of Health’s budget increased from approximately GH¢17.8 billion in 2025 to GH¢22.8 billion in 2026, a 28 per cent nominal increase. The caucus is demanding a detailed account of specific expenditures and allocations for GHIMS and related digital infrastructure, alongside measurable outcomes. Additionally, the Minority has called on the Ministry to review its agreement with Akamai and consider terminating the contract if justified by established facts and contractual provisions.

cards.headline: Russian uranium consignment reaches Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant via alternative route

pages.text: A consignment of uranium imported from Russia for the second unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant (RNPP) reached the project site in Bangladesh at approximately 7:30 am on November 6, 2026. The nuclear fuel was transported in three specially designed trucks using an alternative route to avoid an ongoing garment workers' movement in Gazipur and potential clashes, according to Rooppur project Site In-charge KBM Ruhul Quddus. The convoy entered the site under the supervision of the Bangladesh Army and tight security from other law enforcement agencies. Instead of the usual route via the Dhaka-Tangail Highway and Jamuna Bridge, the convoy traveled from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport through the Dhaka-Mawa Expressway, Padma Bridge, Bhanga in Faridpur, Rajbari, Kushtia, and the Lalon Shah Bridge at Pakshi before arriving at Rooppur.

With this arrival, a total of five uranium consignments have reached the project site, consisting of two additional consignments for the first unit of the RNPP and three for the second unit. In total, nine consignments of nuclear fuel are scheduled to be brought into the country. Previously, Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom announced plans to transport 163 uranium fuel assemblies for the second unit of Rooppur using seven cargo aircraft, as well as 48 assemblies in two cargo flights for refueling the first unit. The RNPP is being constructed using Russian technology and features two VVER-1200 reactor units. The first unit has already begun activities under the 'Power Startup Stage-C' programme, following approval from the Chairman of the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) on October 29.

cards.headline: Guardian Insurance abandons court action after Southdown Institute records were destroyed

pages.text: Guardian Insurance has discontinued a court action seeking to compel the Southdown Institute, a therapy centre for priests, to produce records after the institute revealed the documents were destroyed more than 20 years ago. Lawyers for Guardian Insurance had believed the institute's records could demonstrate that the Diocese of Grand Falls was aware of abusive priests prior to entering into an insurance policy in the 1980s. This evidence was intended for use in a separate court action where the insurer is attempting to avoid covering the Catholic church's liability to abuse survivors in Newfoundland, Canada. Guardian Insurance filed to discontinue the action and agreed to cover the costs incurred by the Southdown Institute.

The legal dispute focused on documentation regarding Father Leonard Joseph Kelly, a priest who was sent to the Southdown Institute in 1970 following unspecified incidents in the rural community of Baie Verte. While the institute confirmed Kelly was admitted in 1970, it could provide no further information. In an affidavit, Southdown Institute interim clinical director Dr. Samuel Mikail stated that the institute does not maintain archives for long-term storage and is not required by any statute or law to maintain clinical or patient records or materials. Mikail noted that the institute adopted a records management policy in 2000 that allowed for the destruction of materials 12 years after the date of the last clinical contact, meaning any files on Kelly would have been erased under that policy.

Although clinical records were destroyed, the Southdown Institute maintains a database indicating when individuals are admitted to and discharged from programming. This database shows that Kelly was admitted three times. Those admission dates correspond with the unspecified allegations in Baie Verte and later allegations that resulted in jail time.

cards.headline: Syrian security forces kill five during raid in Rankous

pages.text: Syrian security forces killed five people and rounded up 45 others during a raid on homes and shops in the town of Rankous on 22 October. The raid occurred in the Qalamoun mountains near the Lebanese border. According to the Ministry of Interior, the victims had links to the Islamic State (IS), held “extremist ideas”, and had “declared the Syrian state as infidel”. Residents reported that three of the victims were unarmed at the time, while two opened fire on security forces, killing two of its members.

cards.headline: Three more people die and 1,535 are hospitalised with dengue in Bangladesh

pages.text: Three more people have died from the mosquito-borne disease dengue and 1,535 others have been hospitalised across Bangladesh over a 24-hour period. According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), these latest fatalities bring the total death toll to 455, which includes 36 deaths recorded during the first five days of November 2026. The DGHS reported that the disease killed 174 people in October and 148 people in September. Of the new hospital admissions recorded between 8am on November 5, 2026, and the following 24 hours, Dhaka Division accounted for 721 cases. cards.headline: Hundreds of garment factories in Bangladesh suspend operations amid wage protests

pages.text: Hundreds of garment factories in Bangladesh have suspended operations as workers continue to protest for higher wages, a development that threatens the country's nearly $40 billion readymade garment (RMG) industry. The industry accounts for approximately 80-84 per cent of Bangladesh's total export earnings and contributed 8.5 per cent to the country's nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in FY25, according to a Bangladesh Bank quarterly review. The sector sustains around four million workers. According to reports from the Bengali daily Prothom Alo, operations were suspended in 414 factories across Gazipur and Savar in the Dhaka district, while other estimates suggest the number of suspended factories could have risen to 500-600. On November 3, the fourth day of protests, demonstrators obstructed the Dhaka-Tangail highway. Protesters are demanding a hike in minimum wages from Tk 12,500 to Tk 30,000, citing severe inflation. As of September, the country's point-to-point annual inflation stood at 8.34 per cent, up from 8.26 per cent in August.

The protests have involved reports of intense clashes between police and protesters, as well as incidents of vandalism in Gazipur, Mirpur, and Savar. At least one worker, 21-year-old Toufiq Sheikh (also reported as Toufiq Hossain) of Laila Garments, died from severe injuries after being attacked while filming vandalism during the wage protests in Gazipur, according to reports. Protesting worker Mahin Hossain stated that the cost of living has skyrocketed, making it difficult to run families on current wages. While the Israeli army had previously warned residents against entering the area encompassing more than half of the village's groves, villagers have continued attempting to harvest the trees because the crops are their primary livelihood. cards.headline: Usibras imports Ivorian kernels to sustain Ghanaian cashew processing operations

pages.text: Usibras, a leading cashew processor in Ghana, has begun importing semi-processed cashew kernels from Côte d’Ivoire to keep its factory operational. The company is importing borma kernels—cashew nuts that have been shelled and dried but still retain their inner skin—to perform final peeling, processing, and packaging within Ghana. This shift follows a period where soaring domestic farm-gate prices and aggressive foreign buying made procuring local raw cashew nuts highly uncompetitive for the processor.

The procurement shortfall has significantly reduced the factory's output. During the last harvest season, Usibras purchased 6,500 tonnes of raw cashew nuts (RCN), which represents 19 per cent of its installed annual processing capacity of 35,000 tonnes. Operating at less than one-fifth of its potential has placed financial strain on the facility, which is one of West Africa's largest cashew processing investments.

Usibras leadership attributes the crisis to regulatory gaps regarding raw exports. Under current trade regulations, raw cashew nuts can be exported from Ghana with minimal restriction, as traders pay a nominal levy of GH¢92 per tonne to the Tree Crops Development Authority (TCDA). This allows foreign buying agents to purchase raw nuts directly from farming communities at aggressive prices. Because these agents export raw materials without adding value, they avoid local costs such as power tariffs, labor, and operational overheads, allowing them to outbid domestic processors that carry heavy capital expenditures for local manufacturing.

cards.headline: Ghana loses an estimated $6.56 billion in annual potential mining revenue

pages.text: Ghana loses an estimated $6.56 billion in potential revenue from its mining sector every year because the government has limited participation in mineral extraction, according to the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS). At a policy briefing in Accra on November 5, 2026, IFS Executive Director Dr. Said Boakye stated that the country has been unable to maximize returns from its mineral resources. He urged authorities to use the upcoming 2027 Budget to address these leakages, which he said have constrained the country's ability to finance development. Dr. Boakye attributed the stronger performance of Botswana to that government's active involvement in its mining sector through partnerships with private companies. In 2025, Botswana generated $13.4 billion in value added from mining, while Ghana's revenue from the sector was $1.6 billion, representing 11.9 per cent of the sector's value. Dr. Boakye noted that if Ghana had generated mining revenue at Botswana’s average rate of 60.9 per cent, the government would have earned $8.16 billion instead of the $1.6 billion collected.

The IFS identified several factors undermining domestic revenue mobilization, including tax evasion, underreporting, tax avoidance, and collusion involving revenue administrators. Dr. Boakye also cited a revelation from April 2026 by Ghana Revenue Authority Commissioner-General Anthony Sarpong, who stated the country lost more than GH¢11 billion in revenue at its ports due to incorrect declarations regarding the valuation, classification, and country of origin of imported goods. Regarding broader economic metrics, the IFS report found that Ghana's total revenue and grants-to-GDP ratio was 15.7 per cent in 2022, compared to an average of 20.1 per cent for 25 sub-Saharan African countries. The institute estimated that if Ghana's revenue-to-GDP ratio had matched the sub-Saharan African average in 2025, it would have collected GH¢288.26 billion in total revenue and grants, rather than the actual collection of GH¢224.88 billion. This performance placed Ghana 18th among the 25 countries examined.

cards.headline: NASA astronauts cast US election votes from the International Space Station

pages.text: NASA astronaut Anil Menon announced that he and colleagues Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins have cast their votes from the International Space Station using a secure electronic system. In a post on X, Menon stated that voting from space is possible, sharing a video of himself in his private cabin—which he referred to as his “polling station”—displaying an “I voted” sticker. Menon explained that he completed the form on his computer and sent it to Harris County, Texas, where his vote was officially recorded. Harris County is the standard electoral destination for NASA astronauts because it contains the Johnson Space Center in Houston, the agency's primary center for managing human spaceflight missions.

The voting process utilizes NASA's existing space communications and navigation infrastructure to transmit data from the station to Earth. To vote, astronauts first request an absentee ballot using the “Federal Post Card Application,” a form also used by US military personnel stationed far from home. Once the astronaut completes the ballot on board, it is transmitted via the “Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System” to a ground antenna at NASA's White Sands facility in Las Cruces, New Mexico. The ballot is then transferred to Mission Control at the Johnson Space Center before being sent to the relevant county election official for registration and counting. NASA states that the process is protected by strict security measures, including encryption that ensures only the astronaut and the authorized election official can see the ballot's contents.

Voting from orbit is a practice that began in 1997 after the Texas legislature passed a law allowing NASA astronauts to vote in US elections while in space. American astronaut David Wolf was the first to cast a vote from orbit in 1997 from the Russian space station Mir. The three astronauts who voted from the International Space Station arrived via two different missions: Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins launched on 1 October as part of SpaceX’s “Crew-13” mission, while Anil Menon arrived in mid-July aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft. They are currently stationed with Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk and Russian cosmonauts Anna Kikina, Pyotr Dubrov, and Sergei Teteriatnikov.

cards.headline: Scientists achieve record-breaking low temperature aboard China's Tiangong space station

pages.text: Researchers from China have achieved a new low-temperature record aboard the Tiangong space station, according to a study recently published in Science. This achievement may enable a new generation of precision measurements and quantum physics experiments in space. At temperatures approaching absolute zero, matter begins to behave differently, creating conditions that allow scientists to study new states of matter and quantum physics. As atoms get colder, they slow down, which allows for more accurate measurements.

The research focuses on creating a Bose–Einstein condensate (BEC), a state where atoms form a cloud that behaves as a shared quantum wave. Researchers describe BECs as versatile platforms for quantum simulation. Achieving these extremely low temperatures is difficult because gravity causes atoms to sag within a trap. While magnetic levitation has been used to counteract gravity, that method forces atoms to maintain the same internal spin state.

cards.headline: Robotic builder completes first autonomous structure assembly in space

pages.text: A robotic truss builder designed by researchers at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) has successfully constructed a structure in space without astronaut assistance for the first time. The demonstration, known as the Autonomous In-Space Tensioned Reflector Assembly (ASTRA), utilized an autonomous manipulator to pick up struts and joints from dispensers to assemble sections of a perimeter truss. This process is part of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Novel Orbital and Moon Manufacturing, Materials, and Mass-efficient Design (NOM4D) program. While the team encountered time limitations and only completed the initial section of the antenna, the demonstration proved the feasibility of an assembly concept that can be scaled to support very large reflective surfaces. The robot spent six months in space working to construct a 1.4-meter-diameter (4.6-foot-diameter) reflector antenna using aluminum joints, composite fiber tubes, and a Kapton reflective surface.

The ASTRA demonstration represents the third phase of the DARPA project. In the first two phases, the ASTRA team developed the design methodology and verified the concept in Earth-based laboratory settings. The space payload was completed, tested, and delivered to the host, Momentus Inc., in less than 12 months. Sergio Pellegrino, a senior research scientist at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and team leader for the ASTRA demonstration, described the development of the complex payload as an enormous undertaking for the small team. Pellegrino also serves as the co-director of the Space Solar Power Project, which seeks to harvest solar power in space and transmit it wirelessly to Earth.

cards.headline: Newly described 'hell chicken' dinosaur may be the first known species to eat mostly fruit

pages.text: Researchers have described a dinosaur species, *Infernogallus jamesi*, that may be the first known dinosaur to have eaten mostly fruit. According to a study published October 10 in the journal *Nature Communications*, the creature possessed a mouth and jaw adapted for chewing soft foods, similar to the way frugivorous parrots eat today. This discovery suggests that dinosaur diets during the Late Cretaceous period were more diverse than previously thought, moving beyond the well-known categories of meat-eating carnivores and large herbivorous sauropods.

The species name *jamesi* honors the grandfather of one of the study's co-authors, while the genus name *Infernogallus* means “hell chicken.” This name refers to the animal's small size and the fact that its fossils—including a partial skeleton and a nearly complete skull—were discovered in the Hell Creek Formation, a fossil site spanning Montana, the Dakotas, and Wyoming. Living approximately 67 million years ago, *I. jamesi* was one of the smallest caenagnathids, a group of feathered, two-legged dinosaurs with beaks. The animal weighed an estimated 25 pounds and was roughly the size of a turkey, living in the same region and time as the *Tyrannosaurus rex*.

Thomas Dudgeon, an evolutionary ecologist at the Royal Ontario Museum in Canada and a study co-author, told Reuters that while it had been proposed previously that some dinosaur groups ate fruit, there had never been evidence to support it. The findings provide new insight into Cretaceous ecology by demonstrating that some dinosaurs took advantage of fruit as a food source between 66 million and 100 million years ago.

cards.headline: Unexpected discovery of baby North Atlantic right whale off Quebec, Canada

pages.text: Researchers in Canada captured images of an unidentified baby North Atlantic right whale, one of the rarest sea mammals in the world, off Anticosti Island in Quebec in September. Scientists with the New England Aquarium in Boston analyzed photos and data to determine the animal was a calf likely born months ago that went unseen during winter surveys for the giant animals. This discovery brings the number of baby right whales discovered from the most recent birthing season to 24.

cards.headline: Reduced Southern Ocean biological pump efficiency may have driven high CO2 during Early Eocene Climatic Optimum

pages.text: Research published in Nature Geoscience suggests that a less efficient biological pump in the Southern Ocean may have explained at least half of the atmospheric CO2 increase observed during the Early Eocene Climatic Optimum. This period, occurring 53 to 49 million years ago, featured reconstructed temperatures and atmospheric CO2 concentrations among the highest of the Cenozoic Era, the last 66 million years of Earth's history. While the exact causes of these high CO2 levels remain unclear, researchers used foraminifera-bound nitrogen isotope measurements to test if the Southern Ocean played a role similar to its function during recent ice age cycles, where biologically mediated carbon build-up and release control CO2 changes.

The study found higher surface nitrate concentrations in the Southern Ocean during the peak of the Early Eocene Climatic Optimum. These higher concentrations indicate a more inefficient biological sequestration of carbon, meaning the ocean's biological pump—the process by which organisms move carbon from the surface to the deep ocean—was less effective at trapping CO2. This inefficiency allowed for the transfer of CO2 from the deep ocean to the atmosphere. This transfer was likely amplified by the low seawater buffering capacity of the Eocene, caused by lower pH and high calcium (Ca) ion concentrations. Additionally, previously proposed low silicate rock weatherability during the Eocene may have weakened the weathering thermostat, a natural process that helps regulate atmospheric CO2.

cards.headline: Neuroimaging study finds dampened brain network reorganization in people with psychiatric diagnoses

pages.text: A neuroimaging study published in Nature Communications indicates that the adaptive shifting of large-scale brain communication networks is dampened, or “flattened,” in people with psychiatric diagnoses. In a healthy human brain, these networks flexibly reorganize to meet the challenges of transitioning from quiet rest to demanding mental tasks. Instead of operating as a fixed circuit board, the brain acts as a dynamic system that continuously adjusts connections to respond to changing demands. This research suggests that these network shifts may align more closely with an individual's specific mix of symptoms than with a formal psychiatric diagnosis. To study how the brain coordinates information, neuroscientists examine functional brain networks, which are groups of distinct regions across the outer cerebral cortex and deeper structures that work together. Scientists use functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI)—a scan that tracks blood flow changes tied to neural activity—to estimate functional connectivity by measuring how closely activity in different brain regions rises and falls in sync.

The study builds on previous research regarding how brain networks move away from a baseline state. While many brain imaging studies rely on static resting-state scans that measure average connectivity while a person lies quietly in a scanner, a 2016 neuroimaging study of healthy young adults demonstrated that brain networks actively reorganize from this baseline during tasks. These networks shift differently for simple motor actions than they do for complex working memory challenges. Additionally, a 2021 study in the Journal of Neuroscience, co-authored by the new study’s lead author Carrisa Cocuzza, indicated that although task-related connectivity shifts are subtle, these individual-specific adjustments improve predictions of brain activity across two dozen cognitive conditions.

Connecting these network shifts to mental illness is complicated because traditional psychiatric diagnoses often group together patients with very different symptom combinations. For example, people with distinct diagnoses like depression and schizophrenia can share problems such as difficulty planning, fatigue, or low motivation. Even individuals without a clinical diagnosis can experience mild or temporary versions of these difficulties, leading researchers to view mental health through broad dimensions of functioning rather than rigid categories. An earlier neuroimaging study of children, adolescents, and adults supported this view, finding that brain connectivity patterns were more consistent within broad symptom categories—such as inward-focused internalizing problems versus outward-focused externalizing behaviors—than between them across development.

cards.headline: Brain signaling protein identified as potential therapeutic target for MEF2C-linked neurological disorders

pages.text: Researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign have identified a specific signaling protein in the brain that may serve as a therapeutic target for neurological disorders caused by deletions of the MEF2C gene. In a mouse study published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the research team explored how the loss of this gene affects protein stability and neurodevelopmental pathology. The findings suggest that targeting the protein PSD-95 could potentially address issues arising from MEF2C mutations, which are linked to autism spectrum disorder, epilepsy, and Alzheimer's disease. Nien-Pei Tsai, an Illinois professor of molecular and integrative physiology and study leader, noted that while MEF2C haploinsufficiency is a rare genetic disorder, the MEF2C protein is associated with many other diseases due to its dysregulation. MEF2C haploinsufficiency occurs when an individual has only one copy of the MEF2C gene instead of the typical two, a condition characterized by seizures, intellectual disability, and autism spectrum disorder.

The study focused on the relationship between MEF2C and the neural signaling protein PSD-95, a protein also associated with Alzheimer's and epilepsy. Tsai, who is also affiliated with the Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology at the University of Illinois, explained that MEF2C has an indirect link to regulating the stability of PSD-95. The research team hypothesized that patients with less MEF2C would experience increased levels of PSD-95 because the protein is not being degraded as it should be. To test this, the researchers bred mice with only one copy of MEF2C to observe the effects of decreasing PSD-95 levels. By investigating this link, the researchers aim to increase knowledge regarding MEF2C and other neurodevelopmental disorders associated with the gene.
